correctness.rationale: On unit-conductance K_{n_1,...,n_k}, the Laplacian acts by N-n_i on within-part contrasts and by N on weighted-zero class-constants, yielding pairwise R=2/(N-n_i) within parts and c(1/d_i+1/d_j) across parts. Decomposing zero-sum coefficients into within-class contrasts z and weighted class sums y gives the exact squared-resistance form -4 sum z_i^2/d_i^2 -4 sum tau_i y_i^2 +2c^2(sum y_i)^2, with sum d_i y_i=0. Positivity of the tau form on the two-constraint kernel, bordered minimization and nonzero Delta leave exactly one possible obstruction. For unequal profiles, Euclidean iff S2/Delta>=c^2/2; equality has one extra null vector, otherwise exactly one negative centered-Gram eigenvalue. Independent exact symbolic Laplacian pseudoinverse and centered R^2 Gram verified examples (1,1,3,5) margin 4941/118600 and inertia (9,0,1), (1,2,2,5) margin -297/16300 and inertia (8,1,1), and four further profiles; p-negative-type comparisons use the finite strictness-below-supremal-exponent theorem. The Gram uses entrywise square R^2, not the conventional unsquared resistance matrix.

originality.rationale: Published pairwise-resistance and unsquared resistance-matrix spectrum results do not imply an all-k exact Euclidean criterion for the resistance metric itself; the universal fact that sqrt(R) embeds in Hilbert space also does not establish embeddability of R. value.rationale: The question whether a natural resistance metric itself (not its square root) is Euclidean is a structural graph-metric classification. A simple exact rational condition, equality rank drop and at-most-one-negative-mode theorem for every k>=3 supply a useful sharp boundary; contrasting ten-vertex examples show dependence on full part profile rather than only largest class.
